title_tag: 10 Best Luxury Hotels in Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Dubai's best 5-star hotels from €233 to €1,041 a night compared on beach, breakfast, room size and score, from Atlantis The Royal to Raffles and Four Seasons.
h1_main: 10 Best Luxury Hotels in Dubai in 2026
author_role: 10 Dubai 5-star hotels compared on nightly price, guest score, beach, breakfast and room size
lead: For most couples the luxury hotel to book in Dubai is Banyan Tree at Bluewaters, €570 a night with breakfast: a 9.5 guest score and 500 m of private beach. The icon everyone searches for, Atlantis The Royal, is €746 with breakfast; the best city hotel is Waldorf Astoria DIFC at €430; and Raffles at €233 gives you a 70 m² room with a terrace for the lowest price here.

The catch most visitors miss: the nightly rate is not what you pay. A 10% service charge, 7% municipality fee, 5% VAT and an AED 20 tourism fee come on top, and only six of the ten include breakfast. All 10 were compared on price for the same night, guest score, beach, breakfast and the size of the cheapest room. Filter by beach, city, families, couples or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Banyan Tree is the first luxury hotel to look at for a Dubai trip where the beach matters. For €570 a night with breakfast included you get 500 metres of private beach on Bluewaters Island, a 54 m² Bliss room with a balcony, and the joint-highest guest score of the ten (9.5).

It is the most balanced resort on the list: guests give it 9.6 for location, facilities and cleanliness and 9.7 for comfort. Dining runs to Demon Duck by Alvin Leung, French Alizée and the all-day Tocha, and the Banyan Tree Spa has a sauna and steam room.

Against Atlantis The Royal (#2) it is €176 cheaper and calmer, but you lose the sky pool, 16 restaurants and the waterpark next door. Against Four Seasons (#4) you save €298 a night and breakfast is already in the price, though Four Seasons' cheapest room is bigger (70 m²) and it suits children better.

The catches: children from 7 pay as adults, there is no kids' club in the listing, and taxes come on top of the €570 (10% service charge, 7% municipality fee, 5% VAT and an AED 20 tourism fee per night).

review: Atlantis The Royal is the showpiece resort on this list. €746 a night buys a 55 m² Seascape King Room with breakfast and free cancellation, a balcony over the sea and access to a resort built for spectacle.

The food is the main event: 16 restaurants and bars, 7 of them from celebrity chefs (Heston Blumenthal, Nobu, Costas Spiliadis of Milos, Gastón Acurio of La Mar) and one with a Michelin star. Add the rooftop sky pool, the private beach and beach clubs, the Skyblaze fountain show, and Aquaventure World next door.

Against One&Only The Palm (#8), it is €284 cheaper, much bigger and far busier; One&Only is the place for privacy. Against Banyan Tree (#1) you pay €176 more for scale and the dining line-up, not for a better score (9.2 against 9.5).

Two rules to know before you book: the minimum check-in age is 21 and there are no extra beds. Taxes, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee come on top, and the half-board rate starts at €898.

review: Waldorf Astoria DIFC is the city luxury pick. €430 a night buys a 49 m² Deluxe King with skyline views, free cancellation and nothing to pay upfront, in the hotel that guests rate highest of all ten for service: 9.8 for staff, cleanliness and comfort, 9.5 overall.

The position is the point: one metro stop from Dubai Mall, Burj Khalifa and Downtown, 11 km from Dubai International. Upstairs is a heated rooftop pool with the St. Trop lounge; downstairs, Bull and Bear, the Cigar Lounge and Peacock Alley with live piano and cello.

Against Address Downtown (#7) it costs €173 less, scores higher (9.5 against 9.0) and gives far better value for money (9.3 against 8.3), but you look at the Burj instead of sitting under it. Against Raffles (#5) you pay €197 more for a smaller room (49 m² against 70 m²) and a fresher, more business-like hotel.
What it does not have is a beach or a big dining scene. Plan beach days elsewhere and add breakfast from €483 if you want it in the rate.

review: Four Seasons Jumeirah Beach is the most complete beach resort for families on this page. €868 a night buys a 70 m² room with a balcony, the biggest entry room of any beach hotel here, with free cancellation and nothing to pay upfront.

It is also the easiest resort for children: free extra beds for 3–17, free cots, programmes for younger guests, consoles on request and no minimum check-in age. The beach is private, with cabanas and day villas, and there are two outdoor pools, an indoor pool, tennis and padel.
The location is a real advantage: on Jumeirah Road, Burj Khalifa and the Dubai Fountain 15 minutes away by car and the Mercury Rooftop bar looking straight at the skyline.

Against Banyan Tree (#1) it costs €298 more and breakfast is extra, so you pay for the room size, the kids' policies and the location. Guests rate it 9.4 overall and 9.7 for staff, cleanliness and comfort.

review: Raffles is where the money goes furthest. €233 a night buys a 70 m² Signature Room with a terrace on a Black Friday deal rate, the same floor space as Four Seasons' entry room at a quarter of the price.

It is a real luxury hotel, not a deal hotel: butler service for every room, a spa with saunas and steam rooms, a rooftop pool plus a kids' pool, and seven dining outlets including TOMO and afternoon tea at Raffles Salon. Guests give it 9.2 overall and 9.5 for staff.

The trade-off is position. It sits by Wafi Mall in Bur Dubai with metro access and is 15 minutes from Dubai International, which is handy for short stays and the old town, but there is no beach and the skyline view is from a distance. Location scores 9.1, joint lowest of the ten with One&Only.
Breakfast is not included at €233. Breakfast-and-dinner rates start at €370 (non-refundable) or €403 with free cancellation.

review: Jumeirah Al Qasr is the Arabian palace version of Dubai luxury: a grand hotel in the Madinat Jumeirah resort on 2 km of private beach, with gardens and the Talise spa's overwater treatment rooms.

It is expensive, €1,041 a night, but the rate does a lot of work: breakfast, unlimited Wild Wadi Waterpark access and the Jumeirah Circle kids' club are included, and extra beds are free for children up to 11. Stay three nights and you add one visit to Dubai Parks and Resorts.

Its sister house Jumeirah Dar Al Masyaf, in the same resort, has rooms in its Arabian Houses from €1,116; Al Qasr is the better pick for families because the kids' club and family pools are here. For a cheaper Jumeirah beach stay with Wild Wadi included, Jumeirah Beach Hotel (#9) costs half as much.
Taxes, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee come on top. Guests score location 9.6 and staff 9.4, but value for money only 8.7.

review: Address Downtown is the hotel for the Burj Khalifa trip. It is a 302-metre, 63-level tower overlooking The Dubai Mall, next to Souk Al Bahar and very near The Dubai Fountain, so the city's big sights are a walk, not a taxi.

€603 a night gets a 55 m² Deluxe Downtown View Room with a dressing area, an L-shaped sofa and a marble bathroom with bathtub and rain shower. There is an outdoor pool, a spa with 9 treatment rooms and the Qix kids' club. If you are going up the tower itself, compare Burj Khalifa tickets before you go.

The weak spot is price. Guests score value for money 8.3, the lowest of the ten, and the flexible rate is €805, with breakfast €40 on top. Waldorf Astoria DIFC (#3) is one metro stop away for €430 with a higher score.
Pick it when location is the whole point of the trip; pick Waldorf or Raffles (#5) when you want more hotel for the money.

review: One&Only The Palm is the private, grown-up end of Dubai luxury. It is a boutique beach resort in Andalusian style with a private sandy beach and gardens, and it was named the Middle East's top resort in the Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2024.

€1,030 a night includes breakfast, free cancellation and waterpark access, in a 65 m² Palm Manor Premier King Room with a balcony. The draw for food lovers is STAY by Yannick Alléno, with two Michelin stars, plus ZEST and 101 for sunset drinks and seafood.

Like Atlantis The Royal, it has a minimum check-in age of 21 and no extra beds. For more Palm options, from family resorts to apartments, see our Palm Jumeirah hotels comparison.

guide.h2: Dubai Luxury Hotels Compared: Price, Score, Beach, Breakfast and Room Size
guide.html:
All ten prices are the lowest nightly rate for two adults on the same January weeknight, before the service charge and taxes. Raffles and Address Downtown were Black Friday deal rates that night and Waldorf Astoria a Late Escape deal. Two columns change the picture: breakfast (six of the ten include it in the cheapest rate) and room size, where the cheapest hotel, Raffles, gives you as much space as Four Seasons at €868.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Luxury Hotel Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best all-round, couples: #1 Banyan Tree, €570 with breakfast. Joint-top score (9.5), 500 m private beach, every room with a balcony.
  • The famous one, food lovers: #2 Atlantis The Royal, €746 with breakfast. 16 restaurants, sky pool, minimum check-in age 21.
  • City break or business: #3 Waldorf Astoria DIFC, €430, one metro stop from Burj Khalifa, best value-for-money score (9.3).
  • Families who want space: #4 Four Seasons, €868: 70 m² rooms and free extra beds to 17. Families who want everything included: #9 Jumeirah Beach Hotel, €521 (breakfast, kids' club, Wild Wadi).
  • Luxury on a budget: #5 Raffles, €233 for a 70 m² room with terrace and butler, or #10 Le Royal Meridien, €312 for the beach with breakfast.
  • Classic Arabian resort: #6 Jumeirah Al Qasr, €1,041, 2 km of beach with breakfast, kids' club and Wild Wadi included.
  • Sightseeing first: #7 Address Downtown, €603, on The Dubai Mall and The Dubai Fountain.
  • Honeymoon or anniversary: #8 One&Only The Palm, €1,030 with breakfast and a two-Michelin-star restaurant downstairs.

Narrowing down by area? Compare our Palm Jumeirah hotels, Downtown Dubai hotels and beach resorts. For a villa or suite with its own pool, see hotels with a private pool, and for smaller, design-led stays, boutique hotels.

guide.h2: Booking a Luxury Hotel in Dubai: Fees, Extras and Location Trade-offs
guide.html:
What the headline price leaves out

  • Service charge: the room rates add a 10% service charge, so Atlantis The Royal's €746 becomes €821 and Le Royal Meridien's €312 becomes €344.
  • Taxes: on top of that come 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee of AED 20 per room per night (AED 40 on some Banyan Tree family rooms), paid at the hotel.
  • Breakfast: included at Banyan Tree, Atlantis The Royal, Al Qasr, One&Only, Jumeirah Beach Hotel and Le Royal Meridien; €40 at Address Downtown; on rates from €483 at Waldorf Astoria.
  • Extra beds: free at Four Seasons (3–17), Al Qasr (to 11) and Banyan Tree (7+); AED 200–400 a night elsewhere; not available at Atlantis The Royal or One&Only.

Beach clubs and waterparks

  • Included in the rate: daily Wild Wadi Waterpark at Al Qasr and Jumeirah Beach Hotel (plus kids' club at both), waterpark access on One&Only's rooms.
  • On site: Atlantis The Royal has beach clubs and sits next to Aquaventure World; Four Seasons has cabanas and day villas for in-house guests.
  • No beach: Waldorf Astoria, Raffles and Address Downtown. Plan a taxi to the coast or a day at a resort.

Beach or city?

  • Palm and Bluewaters (Atlantis The Royal, One&Only, Banyan Tree): the most resort-like, but far from the old town; Atlantis The Royal is 22 miles from Dubai International.
  • Jumeirah coast (Four Seasons, Al Qasr, Jumeirah Beach Hotel): beach plus easier city access; Four Seasons is 15 minutes from Burj Khalifa.
  • City (Waldorf Astoria, Address Downtown, Raffles): walkable sights and short airport runs (Waldorf Astoria is 11 km and Raffles 15 minutes' drive from Dubai International), but beach days need a taxi. Waldorf Astoria and Raffles have metro access.

Age rules

Atlantis The Royal and One&Only The Palm need the person checking in to be 21; most others ask for 18; Four Seasons and Jumeirah Beach Hotel have no minimum age.

Planning the rest of the trip? Compare helicopter tours over the Palm and the coast, and dinner cruises in the Marina for an evening away from the hotel.

faqs.q: What is the best luxury hotel in Dubai?
faqs.a: For most couples, Banyan Tree Dubai at Bluewaters: €570 a night with breakfast, a 9.5 guest score and 500 m of private beach. For a city base, Waldorf Astoria DIFC scores the same 9.5 for €430. The most talked-about resort is Atlantis The Royal at €746 with breakfast.

faqs.q: What is the most luxurious hotel in Dubai you can book?
faqs.a: Of the ten compared, One&Only The Palm (€1,030 with breakfast, two-Michelin-star STAY by Yannick Alléno) and Jumeirah Al Qasr (€1,041 with breakfast, 2 km of private beach) are the most expensive. Atlantis The Royal is the most extravagant, with 16 restaurants and a rooftop sky pool.

faqs.q: How much does a 5-star hotel in Dubai cost per night?
faqs.a: For two adults on a January weeknight, the ten hotels here ran from €233 (Raffles) to €1,041 (Jumeirah Al Qasr), with a median of about €590. Add a 10% service charge, 7% municipality fee, 5% VAT and an AED 20 tourism fee per night.

faqs.q: Which luxury hotels in Dubai include breakfast?
faqs.a: Six of the ten include breakfast in their cheapest rate: Banyan Tree (€570), Atlantis The Royal (€746), Jumeirah Al Qasr (€1,041), One&Only The Palm (€1,030), Jumeirah Beach Hotel (€521) and Le Royal Meridien (€312). At Address Downtown breakfast is €40; at Waldorf Astoria DIFC breakfast rates start at €483.

faqs.q: Which luxury hotel in Dubai is best for families?
faqs.a: Four Seasons Jumeirah Beach for space (70 m² rooms, free extra beds for 3–17), Jumeirah Beach Hotel for value (€521 including breakfast, kids' club and daily Wild Wadi), and Jumeirah Al Qasr for the palace setting with free extra beds to 11. More options in our Dubai family resorts guide.

faqs.q: Should I stay on the beach or in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.a: Stay on the beach (Banyan Tree, Four Seasons, Le Royal Meridien) for a resort holiday, and in the city (Waldorf Astoria DIFC, Address Downtown, Raffles) for sightseeing, shopping and short stays: Waldorf Astoria is one metro stop from Burj Khalifa and Raffles 15 minutes' drive from Dubai International. Four Seasons is the compromise, 15 minutes from Burj Khalifa.

faqs.q: Do Dubai luxury hotels have age limits?
faqs.a: Yes, some. Atlantis The Royal and One&Only The Palm require the guest checking in to be at least 21 and offer no extra beds. Most others require 18, while Four Seasons Jumeirah Beach and Jumeirah Beach Hotel have no minimum check-in age.

methodology: We compared more than 50 of Dubai's top-rated and best-known 5-star hotels on live prices for the same night (two adults, one night in mid-January) and kept the 10 that give a genuinely different choice: Palm and Bluewaters resorts, the Jumeirah beach strip, an Arabian palace and three city hotels, from €233 to €1,041. Each was scored on the nightly price, guest score and location score, whether breakfast is in the rate, beach and pools, the size of the cheapest room, child and age policies, and what costs extra. Rankings reward the best all-round stay first, then the clearest pick for each type of traveller.
